title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial for deaths of her three children in March 2027
description: Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicideLindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her t
body: Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicideLindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a second trial next year, a judge has said. The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face.Prosecutors said they wanted to proceed with a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges, the same as she faced last time. The first trial this year fell apart when the jury failed to reach a verdict over the deaths on 24 January 2023 of five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan at the family home."I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said at Monday's hearing.Clancy was charged in the first trial with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.The district attorney has not yet officially said he will proceed with first-degree-murder charges.The prosecution could choose to bring lesser charges against Clancy, such as second-degree-murder, which applies to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without planning. A week ago, Judge William Sullivan rejected a defence attempt to throw out the case on the grounds of double jeopardy.Double jeopardy is a legal principle that protects someone from being prosecuted more than once for the same crime after an acquittal or conviction. The judge's decision cleared the way for a second trial. It was Judge Sullivan who declared the mistrial on 4 September because of the hung jury.Afterwards, some of the 12 jurors said in media interviews that they had been ready to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but that one juror had held out.It was not disputed at Clancy's first trial that she strangled the children with exercise bands in the basement of the family home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury.She had asked her now-ex husband, Patrick Clancy, to leave the house to pick up takeout food and children's medicine shortly before the children were attacked.But her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. They wanted her found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of criminal responsibility.She is currently in a state-run psychiatric hospital and medical facility in Massachusetts.

schema.headline: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial for deaths of her three children in March 2027

title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
description: Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea susta
body: Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit.The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added.Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people. The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war. The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions.The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences. Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate  has responded to a BBC request for comment. Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation.Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children.Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country.Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect. Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member. The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia. The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement.A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US. But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input. "We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov. EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process".

schema.headline: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war

title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction
description: French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexual assault, admitting that his behaviour towards women had often
body: French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexual assault, admitting that his behaviour towards women had often been offensive and offering a "deep and sincere" apology.On the day that the appeal was due to start in a Paris court, the 77-year-old actor's unexpected mea culpa marks a dramatic reversal of his previous denials of sexual impropriety."Justice was pronounced. I was found guilty. I understand and bow to this conviction… I have therefore decided to abandon the appeal," he wrote.It means he is now guilty in law of abusing two women during a film shoot in Paris five years ago, and his 18-month suspended prison term stands."Victory is ours, and we welcome it with head held high," said one of the two women, named only as Amélie, who was at the court."There is huge relief because the fight is over. The giant of film has fallen," said the other woman in the case, who is known in court by the false name Sarah.In his statement, Depardieu appeared to have undergone a major shift from his earlier stance of unapologetic intransigence."For a long time on film shoots I hid myself behind provocation and smut. I thought that the remarks I made, and certain gestures that I made, were of no consequence."I see now that there is a border between impertinence and offence. Never, ever did I intend to hurt the women with whom I came into contact. But I see now that intention has no bearing on the hurt that people feel."Cases before the courts are damaging. Everything got out of hand… including my defence. Many people have suffered in this story. I have not the power to go back in time. I have come to understand that I belonged to a world that has disappeared."The reference to his defence "getting out of hand" follows widespread criticism of the aggressive line taken by Depardieu's lawyer during the original trial in March last year.

schema.headline: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction

title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
description: Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone
body: Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone factory.Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the break-in on Saturday at a facility north of the capital Tallinn was part of what he called Russia's "broader hybrid war against Europe". The alleged attackers were arrested, Michal said, with local media reporting the suspects are Latvian.They are said to have broken into the factory and attempted to set fire to it using flammable liquids.On Monday, Moscow said the accusation was "baseless" and accused the Estonian government of "building a wall" between the neighbouring countries.The facility targeted is operated by Threod Systems and produces attack and reconnaissance drones, with Ukraine and Nato member states listed as customers on its website. Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that "closing the border crossings will reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia".Michal said "extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures" at the factory, while the head of Estonia's internal security service labelled the incident attempted Russian sabotage.The decision to close border crossings is expected to be finalised next week, according to local media. Estonia shares a border of around 220 miles (338 km) with Russia that spans both sea and land. Three road crossings are in operation but are already subject to restrictions. One of them is located at Narva, Estonia's third biggest city. It sits on the western bank of the River Narva that flows into the Baltic Sea; on the eastern bank is Russia. Closures will complicate life for families which live either side of the border.Kremlin spokesman Dimitry Peskov said: "Estonia is building a wall. Many countries, as history demonstrates, have built walls that have brought nothing good to those who erect such walls."Russia has been repeatedly accused by European leaders of targeting national infrastructure and resources destined for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.Baltic region leaders have repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid attacks and raised fears about the Kremlin's territorial ambitions. Other major backers of Ukraine in Europe, including France, Germany, the UK and Poland, have also said Russia has orchestrated attacks on their soil in recent months.Last year, six men were jailed in the UK over an arson attack linked to Russia at a London warehouse where aid bound for Ukraine was being stored.

schema.headline: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack

title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
description: Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.Germany, Denmark, Austria, Gr
body: Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024.Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights. The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role."IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries.Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo."Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad."The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.Unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, the agency said. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year. In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

schema.headline: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda

title: Avoid this Black Friday scam - how to check it's a real deal
description: If you are self-employed or have more than one source of income you will need to file a tax return by the end of January.Fraudsters seize on this dead
body: If you are self-employed or have more than one source of income you will need to file a tax return by the end of January.Fraudsters seize on this deadline to blitz people with messages that look like they are official and from the UK's tax authority, HMRC.Any such calls or messages should be ignored, but you can also check whether an email, external, text message, external or phone call, external claiming to be from HMRC is genuine."Reporting scams helps us shut them down and protect others," adds Lucy Pike, HMRC's chief security officer.New figures from HMRC, shared with the BBC, show that it received 95,340 reports of suspected scams in the year to the end of October.There were 900 reports of one specific scam which used emails containing a malicious attachment which directed customers to a fake gov.uk webpage designed to steal personal and financial information.To avoid being caught out, HMRC says:it never contacts people by email, text or phone to tell them they are due a refund or ask them to claim oneit never asks for personal or financial information by email or text messageit never leaves threatening voicemails about legal action or arrest

schema.headline: Avoid this Black Friday scam - how to check it's a real deal

title: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
description: US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executiv
body: US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executive called for him to be reinstated.Huang resigned as boss of the AI chip giant last week after the emergence of two affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms, which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion.But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back".The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back."I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive.They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times., externalA representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report.The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House. President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal broke out, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China."They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that." he said.The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping.The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted.Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing.The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation."Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."He added later: "If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through."Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

schema.headline: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched

title: Grammys 2027: Raye leads with 11 nominations as Dolly Parton receives posthumous nods
description: British singer Raye leads the charge at the forthcoming Grammy Awards with 11  nominations, while Dolly Parton has been recognised with three posthumo
body: British singer Raye leads the charge at the forthcoming Grammy Awards with 11  nominations, while Dolly Parton has been recognised with three posthumous nods.Raye is nominated for her latest Mercury-winning record This Album May Contain Hope and its lead single Where Is My Husband!, which is up for both song and record of the year.Other nominees include Rosalía, Ella Langley, Olivia Dean, Ariana Grande, Bruno Mars, Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, Miranda Lambert and Phoebe Bridgers. Parton's two nominations, both in the best country duo/group performance category, come three months after the country music star died aged 80.Parton is recognised for Butterfly, her collaboration with the Zac Brown Band, and Light of a Clear Blue Morning, alongside an all-star line-up including her goddaughter Miley Cyrus.The late country star also received a nomination for best audio book, for her narration of Star of the Show: My Life on Stage.The Grammy Awards 2027 will take place on Sunday 7 February in Los Angeles. See the full nominations list on the official Grammys website, externalThere are five new categories being introduced, including best Latin song and best Asian pop music performance.They have been added as part of the Academy's attempts to make the event "more inclusive" and represent a wider range of music genres.However, critics fear that the new specialist categories will result in genres such as K-pop being under-represented in the major categories, and acts including BTS and Stray Kids have said they will boycott next year's ceremony.Four of Korea’s five biggest entertainment companies withheld their music from consideration. Starship Entertainment, which bucked the trend, scored nominations for its girl bands IVE and KiiiKiii.  The other nominees were Babymetal, Japanese singer Lisa (not to be confused with the Blackpink star of the same name) and the Filipino bands BINI and SB19. Elsewhere, Beyoncé picked up the 100th nomination of her career when Morning Dew (Donk) was shortlisted for best R&B solo performance.Songs and albums had to be released between 31 August 2025 and 28 August 2026 to qualify for nominations. Around 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy are eligible to vote for the winners.

schema.headline: Grammys 2027: Raye leads with 11 nominations as Dolly Parton receives posthumous nods

title: Robert Pattinson: How the Twilight star became 007
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Robert Pattinson has starred in films including the Twilight franchise and The Batman ByHelen BushbyCulture r
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Robert Pattinson has starred in films including the Twilight franchise and The Batman ByHelen BushbyCulture reporterRobert Pattinson's career is already flying high with roles in films including the Twilight series, The Batman and The Odyssey, so signing up to play James Bond will propel his profile into the stratosphere. He's already established himself as a leading man, action star and character actor, which is clearly why he is about to play the suave, British secret agent 007.At 40, he is slightly older than some of the other men reportedly lined up for the role, but he's also the most famous - something the new Bond studio Amazon-MGM may have favoured, with an eye on the box office. His recent work has garnered both critical and box office success, including Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster The Odyssey, in which he played the villainous Antinous.Pattinson was also called "Oscar-worthy" by the Independent and "superb" by The Times, for his performance in November's Primetime, as the real-life host of US TV show To Catch a Predator.He also helped lead 2022's The Batman to the second-biggest North American opening of the Covid-19 pandemic behind Spider-Man: No Way Home. The Guardian said he played the "brooding" role with "appealing vulnerability, external". Meanwhile in dark romantic comedy The Drama, he and his co-star gave a "career-highlight performance", external. It's one of three films he appeared in with Zendaya this year, along with The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Robert Pattinson starred in 2022's The Batman, which was described by critics as a grim, gritty, and gripping super-noirBorn in Barnes, south-west London, Pattinson grew up with his father, a classic car trader and mother, who worked at a modelling agency, and two elder sisters. His interest in acting started while he was still at school, when he joined the Barnes Theatre Club."I wouldn't be acting if it wasn't for that little club," he told Your Local Guardian in 2008, external."I went originally because a lot of pretty girls went there," he said. "I worked backstage and I started acting when all the good people left and I was the only one tall enough to play the lead."In a weird sort of way, that stuff was probably the best I've done and the stuff I am most proud of."He landed his first big film role more than two decades ago, playing Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire. A relatively minor character, but it was enough to get him noticed.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Robert Pattinson and Kristen Stewart starred in five Twilight films from 2005 to 2012Three years later, he had a starring role in the first of five Twilight films, along with Kristen Stewart, in which they played star-crossed lovers - vampire Edward Cullen and mortal-turned vampire Kristen Stewart. Based on Stephanie Meyer's hugely popular young adult books, the films globally grossed more than $3bn (£2.2bn) by 2012, and established Pattinson as a heartthrob. He spoke in his early career of finding his often adoring, screaming fans hard to deal with. "Although is part of the job, it feels like they have been paid to turn up and scream at me at 7.30pm," he said. "Nothing I don't think can prepare you for the fans. I don't know why I'm not getting used to it but I'm completely overwhelmed every time."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Pattinson and Zendaya have appeared in three films together this year - The Drama, The Odyssey and Dune: Part ThreeThe following year though, he was back in big-studio territory, with Odyssey director Christopher Nolan, in sci-fi thriller Tenet, and again in 2022 with The Batman, directed by Matt Reeves and co-starring Zoe Kravitz and Paul Dano.Pattinson told Screen Daily why he returned to big-budget films, explaining: "I guess I was trying to do the opposite of what I've been doing. I started thinking, 'I really want to do a big thing.' "I hadn't done something with a massive budget for ages. But you approach it exactly the same way."The Batman got generally positive reviews, re-establishing Pattinson with a broader range of fans. By 2025, when he was on the red carpet for Parasite director Bong Joon Ho's sci-fi black comedy, Mickey 17, he said it was "quite strange" to have a fanbase that was now dominated by men, external."There's like a bunch of guys, which is a new one for me!" he told the Associated Press.Pattinson's private life has often created interest in the press, not least his previous relationships with Stewart, and then the singer FKA Twigs. Since 2018, he has been in a relationship with model Suki Waterhouse. They got engaged in December 2023 and had their first child, a daughter, in March.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Robert Pattinson and Suki Waterhouse have been a couple since 2018With his latest role as James Bond, Pattinson will be extremely busy, not least because the forthcoming Batman sequel is reportedly due out in 2028. But the actor will have a head start as 007, having already worked with Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve, who also helmed Dune: Part Three. Pattinson was full of praise for him on their most recent film, despite the strain of working in the furnace-like heat of the desert. "The scale of this stuff is just unbelievable, you're having your own Dune theme park, where the gimbal is going upside down and flying, and this is not like work at all," he told the New York Times, external."There are no negatives. Apart from having your sweat drained out of the top of your head, and getting like bulbous sweat bubbles. But even then, I didn't even really notice them. "He's so easy to work with, Denis, it's never really a stress."Sounds like Pattinson will have the cool head needed to juggle his forthcoming roles - including James Bond. You could even say he may end up being shaken, but not stirred.

schema.headline: Robert Pattinson: How the Twilight star became 007

title: UK has lost more than it gained from Brexit, Burnham expected to say
description: The prime minister is expected to argue the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit la
body: The prime minister is expected to argue the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday, Andy Burnham will compare the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at Friday's summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.The Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".Separately Burnham has said he wants to examine the "pros and cons" of different options for Britain's long-term relationship with the EU.Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told the BBC the prime minister would lay out these potential options after the UK-EU summit.However, Burnham has ruled out major changes before the next general election.Burnham is expected to say on Monday: "It's like the emperor's new clothes – where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on."The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained."Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham will set out three tests for any agreement.Firstly, that it must be consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledge that there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement".He will also say it must improve the original Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.Finally, he will say any deal must pass the "Makerfield test" of providing tangible improvements to people's everyday lives - a reference to voters in Burnham's Greater Manchester constituency.He will say the prospect of a new deal is a "win-win" and illustrates a "new approach"."Not adversarial. No longer burning bridges. But being constructive and positive - showing that we can come together to confront shared challenges."As a candidate in the Makerfield by-election that propelled his return to Parliament, Burnham had promised not to "re-run" Brexit arguments and said he was "not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU".However, since becoming prime minister he has said he wants to explore a different long-term relationship with the bloc.He has suggested potential options for the future could range from no changes to the UK-EU relationship, to rejoining the customs union, the single market or a fresh referendum on full EU membership.The prime minister has stressed any changes would require a mandate from the public at a general election.Boris Johnson, who was prime minister when the UK left the EU in 2020 and negotiated the original Brexit deal, has warned Burnham against "wasting his premiership" on Europe.He told the Daily Telegraph, external he believed the public would back Brexit again if Burnham forced another vote on the issue."It is madness to escalate the Brexit issue as your political priority," Johnson told the paper."He will impale himself and his party on this point, and he needs to move off it because he won't win – because the reality is that people are not fools."Deputy Conservative leader Alex Burghart accused Burnham of "reopening a debate the country settled long ago, while ignoring the challenges facing Britain today".Reform UK has said one of the "key benefits" of Brexit is that Britain no longer has to "adhere to ridiculous EU rules", and argued that any form of alignment could have a negative impact on the country's trade policy.The Liberal Democrats have said the draft deal on food exports is a "patch, not a fix" and that the "real solution is to re-join the single market and to establish a customs union with the EU".The Green Party of England and Wales has called for the UK to re-join the customs union, with leader Zack Polanski previously saying "full membership of the EU remains the best option for the UK".

title: Create more jobs for under-25s by cutting National Insurance, key report urges
description: Her workforce has more than halved to 21 staff. Osborne told the BBC it costs "around £60,000 to train an apprentice before we can actually start allo
body: Her workforce has more than halved to 21 staff. Osborne told the BBC it costs "around £60,000 to train an apprentice before we can actually start allowing them onto customers' heads".She said she has had parents so desperate for their children to find employment at her salons that some have even offered to pay their wages."I'm inundated with applications - and I mean inundated - which is heartbreaking because I can't take them on," she said.Osborne does not feel she is getting help to offer jobs to youngsters. "I feel like the government's foot is firmly on my neck," she said. "They promise breathing space. I feel suffocated, suffocated by employment costs."The independent report by former Labour minister Alan Milburn has been in the works for a year and will be published on Tuesday in full.He has already unveiled some of his proposals including:Reducing benefits - under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide Universal Credit or personal independence payment (Pip), which is the main disability benefit in England and WalesA legal guarantee of a job, training or employment support with those who refuse to take up potentially losing their benefits.Doubling the threshold at which businesses start paying NI for 21 to 24-year-olds from £5,000 to £10,000.At the moment, businesses pay no employer NI contributions for workers younger than 21 or for apprentices under 25 – unless they earn above a threshold of  £50,270.However, for non-apprentices aged 21-24, employers pay 15% on annual earnings above £5,000.This has been the situation since April 2025, after the then Chancellor Rachel Reeves increased the rate from 13.8% and lowered the threshold from £9,100.Under Sir Keir Starmer, the government raised NI for firms but Milburn will say the Neets issue was not started by the increase.Immediately axing NI for 21 to 24-year-olds would cost £5.1bn, according to research by the Resolution Foundation, a left-leaning think tank.Milburn is set to say that an immediate across-the-board cut in employer NI is not the best use of several billions of pounds of public money.But shadow work and pensions secretary, Helen Whately, said the government should "just stop doing the taxing".Milburn told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg programme he supported the government subsidising wages to encourage businesses to take on young workers. "Because young people today are walking into the workplace often with a mental health problem, ADHD or anxiety, if you're a small business that's a cost that you've got to absorb," he said."The state has a responsibility to help them with that."On Sunday, Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the government would extend its subsidised jobs guarantee scheme for 18 to 24-year-olds who are claiming Universal Credit. People who have been on benefits for 12 months will be eligible, down from 18 months and the scheme would be available for people in England, Scotland and Wales.McFadden said the scheme, which guarantees workers a six-month job, "will help more than 90,000 young people into work by March 2029".Additional reporting by Ollie Smith and Anuk Weerawardana

schema.headline: Create more jobs for under-25s by cutting National Insurance, key report urges

title: England v New Zealand: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie says team 'let the country down' in Wales defeat
description: Rennie paid tribute to a "clinical and passionate" Wales team, but he lamented his side's uncharacteristic wastefulness when camped in Welsh territory
body: Rennie paid tribute to a "clinical and passionate" Wales team, but he lamented his side's uncharacteristic wastefulness when camped in Welsh territory in the final quarter of the game."We are all reflecting on what we could do better. You can't just blame it on the guys who take the field," Rennie said."It's disappointing and not good enough, but we've got to learn from it and bottle up the feeling post-game, because it hurts, and we have some pretty big footy coming up in the next few weeks and next year."I should have done a better job last week. We picked a side that was a very good side and a side I was really confident that if we played to our potential would perform well."But I also knew [Wales] had a really strong coaching group, smart, and were a passionate nation playing at home."Rennie is set to call upon a host of big-name players for the match at Allianz Stadium as the All Blacks look to avenge their defeat in Twickenham this time last year.Damian McKenzie, Jordie Barrett, Codie Taylor and Cam Roigard will all return, while star wing Will Jordan is in the selection mix after a hamstring problem.However, Quinn Tupaea, a fixture in the team throughout 2026 at outside centre, needs surgery on a thumb injury and will be out for the next 10 weeks."Playing England at Twickenham is always a big occasion, and we are playing a side who is in good form," added Rennie."They can hurt you up front, they bring a lot of line speed defensively, and they've been really sharp attack-wise. They are playing a lot of footy and we are well aware of that."The loss on the weekend creates a little bit more edge, but I wouldn't say we are going to be more motivated than we would have been. England at Twickenham is always a tough assignment."

title: Has James Trafford replaced Jordan Pickford as England No 1?
description: Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.Trafford returned to his boyhoo
body: Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a £31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for £45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice. "Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him."Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes."After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management."This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard. Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.What about Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.The 32-year-old has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton."We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," said former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period."This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much."I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection."This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

schema.headline: Has James Trafford replaced Jordan Pickford as England No 1?

title: Thomas Frank: How former Spurs boss could restore his reputation and save Crystal Palace
description: "When the time is right I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication," said Thomas Frank i
body: "When the time is right I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication," said Thomas Frank in June.That time is now after the Dane was confirmed as the new boss of Crystal Palace, who are two points and a goal difference deficit away from safety at the bottom of the Premier League.Former head coach Pierre Sage was sacked last week after just 16 league and cup games.The role offers Frank an opportunity to rebuild his reputation after he was sacked by Tottenham in February after eight months.Frank described it as "an honour" to be "in charge of this fantastic football club" as Palace announced his arrival."Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League," Frank told Palace's website."I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."Palace chairman Steve Parish said Frank was the "perfect fit for our club".But how big is the challenge at Selhurst Park that awaits the man who made his name at Brentford?"It's going to be a bit of a shock for Thomas Frank," former West Ham and England goalkeeper Rob Green tells BBC Sport."He had his success at Brentford - a very well-run club where players are brought in with a lot of thinking and planning to take over the players they sell for profit."That doesn't happen at Crystal Palace."They lose players and then have a mad scramble to get players in. They have a team that has been decimated by sales and not replaced by the same quality."Thomas Frank needs to find something within that team that builds and garners the belief that means that they can compete in the Premier League, because it feels a long way short of that right now."Will Frank prove the right fit for Palace and haul the Eagles out of the relegation zone?Since getting the sack at Tottenham after 26 league games last season, Frank has been out of management longer than he was in charge of Spurs.In the summer he released a statement in which he said "there have been conversations and opportunities" to return to management, but that he had "decided not to rush into the next role".Frank's name was heavily linked with Palace before they went for a head coach with no Premier League experience to replace Oliver Glasner - the man who delivered an FA Cup, a Conference League title and Community Shield before moving to Nottingham Forest."Palace had one of the best managers they have had, if not forever, silverware coming across the doorstep. Look at what they achieved last season and instead of building on that, they dismantled a team," said former Tottenham and England goalkeeper Paul Robinson."They have regressed."Frank once described managing as being on a "hamster wheel" and a "crazy circus"., externalHIs coaching staff will include current assistant manager Paddy McCarthy and goalkeeping coach Andy Quy, who previously worked with him at Brentford.So why does he feel now is the right moment to return to management at a club propping up the table?Frank, who was part of BBC Sport's World Cup punditry team during the summer, will be coming into the job refreshed and with renewed energy and enthusiasm following several months out of the game.Between his appointment as Brentford boss in October 2018 and the sack at Tottenham earlier this year, he managed without a break for seven years and four months.Spending the past few months away from Premier League pressure has allowed Frank, in his own words, to "study, observe and learn from other leaders both within sport and beyond".Will his positivity and passion rub off on a Palace team who have lost seven times in 10 top-flight matches?Frank, who places a major emphasis on set-piece organisation, will have to hit the ground running at Palace, who have lost their past four league games.They have conceded more goals than anyone else in the Premier League (24) and have scored only 10 themselves."If you want someone to go in and restore some stability and defensive solidity while improving the set-piece element of the team, then Thomas Frank is the perfect man for the job," Times football writer Tom Allnutt told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily podcast.With the Premier League season just 10 games old, Frank certainly has time to turn it around and will have targets in mind when the transfer window opens in January.Palace sold France centre-back Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for £52m and Colombia right-back Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest for £22m during the summer transfer window.Allnutt added: "We know they have sold so many good players and so far I don't think they have really replaced them adequately."Another challenge for Frank is getting midfielder Adam Wharton, who has not played for England since March, back to something like his best form.These are all challenges the new manager will relish.After his bruising experience at Tottenham - having established Brentford in the Premier League - Frank has decided to climb back on the hamster wheel with Palace."Crystal Palace and Thomas Frank feels like a very good fit," added Robinson.

schema.headline: Thomas Frank: How former Spurs boss could restore his reputation and save Crystal Palace
